source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 24ης Απριλίου — «Άγιος Δούκας ο ράπτης από τη Μυτιλήνη»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 24 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The page makes him a Mytilenean working as a tailor in a shop at Constantinople, flayed alive there on 24 April 1564 — the same day the calendar keeps him — after the wife of a Turkish grandee slandered him to the vizier. It names no judge but the vizier and the eparch, and it prints no hymn and no relic. The corpus holds nobody else of this name.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 07.05.2026 (24. април ст. ст.) — „Св. новомуч. Лука и Никола.“

attestations.note: **An identification, and it is a reading.** The Prologue calls this new martyr Лука, Luke, where saint.gr and this folder call him Δούκας, Doukas. Everything else in the two lines is the same man: a tailor by trade („кројач по занату“ against «ο ράπτης»), a youth, a new martyr, dead in **1564**, commemorated on **this same menologion day**. The corpus holds no other new martyr of either name on 24 April. So the row is written here rather than as a second folder, and the name difference is recorded rather than resolved: this reader did not change the folder's English name, and whether Лука is a rendering of Δούκας or a second tradition about his name is the author's.
